reference.label: Transmit laser failure
reference.definition: A hard transmitter-laser fault that removes the optical channel seen by the remote receiver.
reference.example: A transponder laser stops emitting, causing EQPT_TX_FAIL locally and OCH_LOS remotely.

reference.label: Card failure
reference.definition: A hard card-level equipment failure that interrupts traffic or telemetry and may mask derivative traffic alarms.
reference.example: An OTN line card fails, raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL, and stops reporting performance data.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: A local receiver impairment that raises errors while the optical path and other channels can remain normal.
reference.example: One coherent receiver reports high pre-FEC BER despite normal channel power and healthy neighboring channels.

reference.label: Transmit laser ageing
reference.definition: Gradual transmitter-laser deterioration evidenced by increasing bias current before loss of optical output.
reference.example: Laser bias rises to 121% of its beginning-of-life value before the transmitter fails.

reference.label: Channel margin erosion
reference.definition: A gradual reduction in a channel's performance headroom, commonly from cumulative ageing along its path.
reference.example: A channel's measured margin declines from 4 dB to 1.5 dB over several months.

reference.label: Fibre break
reference.definition: A physical discontinuity in a fibre section that prevents optical propagation.
reference.example: A cable cut leaves the next amplifier input dark and raises AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: Optical amplifier failure
reference.definition: A hard failure of an optical amplifier that leaves it unable to produce usable output light.
reference.example: An inline amplifier loses its pump and all downstream wavelengths disappear.

reference.label: Disconnected optical jumper
reference.definition: An open optical connection caused by removal or unseating of a jumper or patch cord.
reference.example: A technician unplugs the multiplex-section input jumper, leaving the preamplifier without light.

reference.label: Blocked ROADM port
reference.definition: A ROADM port state that prevents selected incoming light from passing onward.
reference.example: A closed ROADM ingress blocks a wavelength and causes OCH_LOS at its receiver.

reference.label: Excess fibre loss
reference.definition: Abnormally high attenuation in a fibre section that reduces delivered power and optical margin.
reference.example: A damaged splice adds 10 dB of span loss and eventually causes an amplifier input-loss alarm.

reference.label: Amplifier noise degradation
reference.definition: An amplifier impairment that lowers OSNR even though signal and output power may remain present.
reference.example: An ageing amplifier holds target output power but adds enough noise to cause OTU_SD.

reference.label: Differential group delay increase
reference.definition: An increase in polarization-mode delay that exceeds coherent-receiver compensation margin.
reference.example: A polarization event raises DGD and eventually causes OTU_LOF while light remains present.

reference.label: WSS passband misalignment
reference.definition: Spectral displacement of a WSS passband from its channel, degrading quality despite potentially normal measured power.
reference.example: A WSS filter shifts 5 GHz off-center, increasing pre-FEC errors without reducing channel power.

reference.label: Fast polarization transient
reference.definition: A state-of-polarization change faster than the coherent receiver can track.
reference.example: A fibre disturbance produces a rapid polarization rotation and a burst of errored seconds.

reference.label: Contaminated optical connector
reference.definition: Connector contamination that introduces optical loss or reflection and degrades signal quality.
reference.example: Dust on a patch-panel connector raises pre-FEC BER enough to trigger OTU_SD.

reference.label: Unspecified failure
reference.definition: A failure known to affect the relevant component or path but not assigned a more specific defect class.
reference.example: PROT_ACTIVE is attributed to an unspecified failure on the working ODU path.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: An amplifier deficiency in which achieved gain falls below its configured target.
reference.example: An amplifier set for 20 dB gain produces only 17 dB and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: Amplifier pump ageing
reference.definition: Gradual pump-laser wear requiring increasing drive current to maintain amplifier gain.
reference.example: Pump current climbs above 120% of its beginning-of-life value and triggers AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: Amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: A wavelength-dependent gain imbalance that makes channels near one band edge weaker than others.
reference.example: The highest-frequency channels leave an amplifier 3 dB weaker than center-band channels.

reference.label: Amplifier pump failure
reference.definition: Failure of an amplifier's pump laser that prevents the unit from providing its intended optical output.
reference.example: A preamplifier has valid input light but no output after its pump stops.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: A hard fault in an OTN cross-connect fabric that disrupts traversing ODUs and client services.
reference.example: An OTN switch fabric fails and forwards ODU-AIS on every affected connection.

reference.label: Wrong ODU cross-connection
reference.definition: An OTN provisioning error that routes an ODU to an unintended destination without requiring an optical-layer fault.
reference.example: An ODU is mapped to the wrong client egress and the receiving port raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: A hard hardware failure of a client-facing port that interrupts its associated service.
reference.example: A failed 100GE port raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL and takes its client service down.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: A gradual increase above configured attenuation for one WSS-routed channel.
reference.example: A WSS configured for 3 dB drifts to 7 dB, leaving the channel weak downstream.

reference.label: WSS input-port failure
reference.definition: A hard WSS input failure that blocks every channel entering through that port while other inputs remain operational.
reference.example: The west-degree WSS input fails, blocking its wavelengths while north-degree traffic continues.

reference.label: No light at receiver
reference.definition: No detectable optical signal is present at a line receiver input.
reference.example: A fibre cut leaves the coherent receiver input dark.

reference.label: Optical loss-of-signal defect
reference.definition: The receiver-declared optical loss-of-signal defect caused by input below its detection criterion.
reference.example: Receiver power falls below the LOS threshold and the unit declares dLOS.

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: The receiver cannot recover valid OTU framing, whether light is absent or severely impaired.
reference.example: Severe OSNR degradation destroys frame lock while optical light remains present.

reference.label: Card hardware fault
reference.definition: A detected internal card defect that can disrupt traffic and suppress derivative traffic alarms.
reference.example: A card ASIC fault causes dEQ and raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: Traffic-alarm masking
reference.definition: Suppression of derivative traffic alarms because an equipment alarm already identifies the primary failure.
reference.example: OTU framing alarms are hidden after EQPT_CARD_FAIL is asserted.
synonyms: traffic alarms masked by equipment alarm

reference.label: Optical signal degradation
reference.definition: A present but degraded signal exhibiting low power, poor OSNR, high DGD, filtering penalty, receiver penalty, or reduced margin.
reference.example: A narrowed passband first raises OTU_SD and later causes OTU_LOF.

reference.label: Pre-FEC errors above threshold
reference.definition: Receiver pre-FEC errors exceed the degradation criterion while framing may remain recoverable.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER reaches 2×10^-3 and OTU_SD is raised.

reference.label: Polarization change beyond tracking rate
reference.definition: The received polarization changes faster than the coherent DSP can follow.
reference.example: A rapid SOP rotation exceeds receiver tracking and creates errored seconds.
synonyms: fast SOP change beyond tracking speed

reference.label: Errored seconds
reference.definition: One-second performance intervals containing one or more qualifying transmission errors.
reference.example: A polarization transient produces five errored seconds in a 15-minute bin.

reference.label: ODU-AIS insertion
reference.definition: Generation of ODU alarm indication signal on affected ODUs toward downstream endpoints.
reference.example: After OTU frame loss, the receiver inserts ODU-AIS on every contained ODU.

reference.label: ODU-AIS forwarding
reference.definition: Transparent onward transmission of an already present ODU-AIS through an OTN cross-connect.
reference.example: An ODU entering a switch with AIS leaves the switch with AIS still present.

reference.label: OTU backward defect transmission
reference.definition: Transmission of OTU BDI toward the source to report a forward-direction OTU defect.
reference.example: A receiver that loses frame sends BDI to the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: Laser off
reference.definition: A transmitter state in which its laser produces no usable optical channel.
reference.example: A disabled transmitter laser has zero channel output.

reference.label: Traffic loss
reference.definition: Traffic presented to or received by the affected equipment is no longer recoverable.
reference.example: A failed receive card stops recovering its incoming service traffic.

reference.label: Monitoring unavailable
reference.definition: The affected equipment ceases providing expected telemetry, status, or performance data.
reference.example: A failed card stops updating power and BER counters.

reference.label: Normal operation
reference.definition: The referenced path, channel, or equipment remains within normal operational limits.
reference.example: One receiver reports errors while neighboring channels remain normal.

reference.label: Rising transmit-laser bias
reference.definition: An upward trend in transmitter-laser bias current needed to maintain optical output.
reference.example: Normalized laser bias rises from 100% to 115% over six months.

reference.label: Transmit-laser bias above 120%
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life reference.
reference.example: A normalized bias reading of 122% triggers LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

reference.label: Transmit-laser fault detected
reference.definition: Internal diagnostics identify a fault in the current unit's transmit laser.
reference.example: The card detects absent laser output despite an enable command.

reference.label: Constant-gain amplifier mode
reference.definition: An amplifier control mode that adjusts pump drive to maintain configured gain as input power varies.
reference.example: An inline amplifier increases pump current after its input level falls.

reference.label: Weak amplifier input
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power arriving at an amplifier is below its expected level.
reference.example: A 5 dB upstream loss leaves the inline amplifier input weak.

reference.label: Weak amplifier output
reference.definition: Aggregate amplifier output power is below its expected target across carried channels.
reference.example: Composite output is 4 dB below target and every downstream wavelength is weak.

reference.label: OSNR degradation
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio is reduced, potentially even after signal power has been restored.
reference.example: A node restores channel power but a 2 dB OSNR penalty remains.

reference.label: No amplifier input light
reference.definition: An optical amplifier receives no detectable traffic light at its input.
reference.example: A span cut leaves an inline amplifier input dark.

reference.label: No amplifier output light
reference.definition: An amplifier produces no detectable output light, regardless of whether its input is present.
reference.example: A failed line amplifier emits no light on its output fibre.

reference.label: Input present but output absent
reference.definition: An amplifier has detectable input light but no output, localizing the failure within that amplifier.
reference.example: A preamplifier measures normal input and zero output before raising AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: Power normal after levelling
reference.definition: Optical power is restored to target by node control even though quality penalties may persist.
reference.example: The ROADM restores nominal channel power but cannot recover lost OSNR.

reference.label: Low channel power
reference.definition: A particular wavelength is measured below its expected optical power.
reference.example: A channel expected at -10 dBm is measured at -17 dBm downstream.

reference.label: Impairment passed through
reference.definition: A signal impairment traverses a transparent node without being corrected or regenerated.
reference.example: Low OSNR entering a ROADM remains on the wavelength leaving it.

reference.label: OSC not received
reference.definition: The incoming optical supervisory channel is not detected on a fibre section.
reference.example: A span cut makes the downstream amplifier report OSC absent.

reference.label: OSC failure confined to one section
reference.definition: Loss of an incoming OSC terminates at the receiving site and does not become the same defect on the next section.
reference.example: OSC is lost on A–B while the regenerated OSC on B–C remains operational.

reference.label: All optical channels lost
reference.definition: Every wavelength in the affected optical aggregate is absent.
reference.example: A dead line amplifier removes all 80 channels from its outgoing span.

reference.label: Pump current rising to hold gain
reference.definition: An amplifier increases pump-laser current to preserve configured gain as the pump ages.
reference.example: Pump drive rises from 100% to 118% while gain remains at 20 dB.

reference.label: Amplifier gain outside tolerance
reference.definition: Measured amplifier gain differs from its configured target by more than 2 dB.
reference.example: Measured gain is 17 dB against a 20 dB target.
synonyms: gain more than 2 dB from target

reference.label: Pump current above 120%
reference.definition: Pump-laser drive current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: Normalized pump current reaches 123% and triggers AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: Band-edge channels weak
reference.definition: A spectral subset, commonly near one band edge, has lower power than the remaining channels.
reference.example: The highest-frequency wavelengths arrive 3 dB weaker than center-band channels.
synonyms: channels at one band edge low

reference.label: Misdirected ODU
reference.definition: A single ODU is delivered to an unintended endpoint by an incorrect cross-connection.
reference.example: An ODU intended for port A emerges on port B.

reference.label: ODU trail-trace mismatch
reference.definition: The received ODU trail identifier differs from the provisioned expected identifier.
reference.example: A port expecting CLIENT_A receives CLIENT_B and raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: Client service unavailable
reference.definition: The customer-facing traffic service is interrupted or unavailable.
reference.example: A switch-fabric failure makes the associated Ethernet service unavailable.

reference.label: No optical symptom
reference.definition: An ODU-layer defect exists while optical power and optical-layer framing remain normal.
reference.example: A wrong ODU mapping raises ODU_TIM despite normal channel power.

reference.label: SNCP protection configured
reference.definition: A service has distinct working and protection ODU paths selected at the receiving endpoint.
reference.example: A client is provisioned over disjoint working and protection ODUs.

reference.label: Defect-free protection path available
reference.definition: At least one protected ODU path is free of detected defects and available to the selector.
reference.example: The working path fails, but the selector switches to a healthy protection path.
synonyms: selector can choose a healthy path

reference.label: Brief protection-switch hit
reference.definition: A protected service experiences only a short interruption during path switchover.
reference.example: Traffic is interrupted for 40 ms before resuming on protection.
synonyms: service takes only a brief hit

reference.label: Protection path selected
reference.definition: The protection selector currently forwards traffic from the protection ODU path.
reference.example: A working-path defect causes selection of the protection leg.

reference.label: Protection path unavailable
reference.definition: The standby ODU path is defective and cannot provide protection.
reference.example: Traffic remains on working while a cut on the standby path raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

reference.label: Port hardware fault
reference.definition: An internal hardware defect prevents reliable operation of a client-facing port.
reference.example: A failed Ethernet PHY causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: Switch-fabric fault
reference.definition: A detected internal defect in an OTN switch's ODU cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: A failed fabric plane causes OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

reference.label: WSS passband shifted
reference.definition: A WSS filter's passband center is displaced from the channel carrier frequency.
reference.example: The filter center shifts 4 GHz and clips one side of the signal spectrum.

reference.label: WSS passband narrowed
reference.definition: A WSS filter's usable bandwidth is smaller than intended and clips the channel spectrum.
reference.example: A nominal 50 GHz passband narrows to 38 GHz.

reference.label: WSS input blocked
reference.definition: Every channel entering through the affected WSS input is prevented from passing.
reference.example: A failed west-degree input blocks all wavelengths arriving from the west.

reference.label: Other ROADM inputs unaffected
reference.definition: Channels entering through ROADM inputs other than the failed one continue operating normally.
reference.example: The west input fails while north- and east-degree traffic remains in service.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a receiver or receive interface.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports -13.2 dBm received power.

reference.label: Per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for each wavelength by a channel monitor.
reference.example: A monitor reports channel 21 at -3 dBm and channel 22 at -6 dBm.

reference.label: Optical signal-to-noise ratio
reference.definition: The measured or estimated optical signal-to-noise ratio of a wavelength channel.
reference.example: A channel monitor reports 18.5 dB OSNR.

reference.label: Pre-FEC bit-error ratio
reference.definition: Bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction at the line receiver.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports pre-FEC BER of 8×10^-4.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: The measured propagation-time difference between principal polarization modes.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring reports 35 ps DGD during a polarization event.

reference.label: Polarization change rate
reference.definition: The measured rate of change of the received signal's state of polarization.
reference.example: A receiver records a polarization-rate spike coincident with errored seconds.

reference.label: Errored-seconds counter
reference.definition: A performance counter recording seconds containing qualifying errors, commonly in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: A client port records 12 errored seconds in a 15-minute interval.

reference.label: Transmit-laser bias current
reference.definition: Transmitter-laser bias current, commonly normalized to its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A transponder reports laser bias at 121% of beginning-of-life current.

reference.label: Composite amplifier input power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power of all wavelengths entering an amplifier.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports -18 dBm total input power.

reference.label: Composite amplifier output power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power of all wavelengths leaving an amplifier.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports +2 dBm total output power.

reference.label: Normalized pump drive current
reference.definition: Amplifier pump-laser drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: The amplifier reports pump drive at 118%.

reference.label: OSC receive status
reference.definition: Status indicating whether the incoming optical supervisory channel is detected.
reference.example: After a span cut, OSC receive status changes to absent.

reference.label: Client unavailable seconds
reference.definition: A performance counter recording seconds during which the client service is unavailable.
reference.example: A failed port accumulates 60 unavailable seconds during a one-minute outage.

reference.label: Transponder
reference.definition: A transport unit mapping a client signal to and from a single line-side optical wavelength.
reference.example: A 400G transponder carries one 400GE client over a coherent channel.

reference.label: Muxponder
reference.definition: A transport unit multiplexing multiple client signals into a higher-rate line signal.
reference.example: A 400G muxponder aggregates four 100GE clients onto one line channel.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A card that terminates an OTU and exposes or transports its contained ODUs.
reference.example: A 400G OTN line card terminates an OTU4 and presents its ODUs to a switch.

reference.label: Optical amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplification unit used as a booster, intermediate line amplifier, or preamplifier.
reference.example: An EDFA reports composite input, output, and normalized pump current.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier at the transmitting end of a multiplex section that raises launch power.
reference.example: A booster after the ROADM raises the aggregate before the outgoing span.

reference.label: Line amplifier
reference.definition: An intermediate-site amplifier that restores multiplex power between terminal nodes.
reference.example: An inline amplifier supplies 18 dB gain at a mid-span hut.

reference.label: Preamplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier at the receiving end of a multiplex section that raises incoming power before demultiplexing.
reference.example: A preamplifier boosts the incoming line before the ROADM.

reference.label: OTN cross-connect switch
reference.definition: An OTN device whose internal fabric cross-connects ODUs between interfaces.
reference.example: An OTN switch routes an ODU4 from a line card to a client port.

reference.label: Client interface port
reference.definition: A client-facing physical or logical service interface on transport equipment.
reference.example: A 100GE client port terminates a customer's Ethernet connection.

reference.label: CDC ROADM
reference.definition: A reconfigurable optical node that independently routes wavelength channels without fixed color, direction, or contention constraints.
reference.example: A CDC ROADM switches one wavelength east and another south.

reference.label: WSS degree module
reference.definition: A wavelength-selective-switch module serving one ROADM line direction or degree.
reference.example: A four-degree ROADM uses separate WSS modules for its four directions.

reference.label: OCH_LOS
reference.definition: A critical optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm raised when a line receiver has no detectable channel light.
reference.example: A fibre cut leaves a transponder receiver dark and raises OCH_LOS.

reference.label: OTU_LOF
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating that valid OTU frame alignment cannot be recovered.
reference.example: Severe OSNR degradation causes OTU_LOF while light remains present.

reference.label: OTU_SD
reference.definition: A minor OTU signal-degrade alarm raised when receiver errors exceed the degradation threshold.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER and triggers OTU_SD.

reference.label: OTU_BDI
reference.definition: A non-alarming status indicating that the far end reports a defect in the locally transmitted OTU.
reference.example: The remote receiver loses frame and the local transmitter records OTU_BDI.

reference.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating a detected failure of the local transmit laser.
reference.example: A transmitter detects zero laser output and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating a card-level hardware failure.
reference.example: An OTN card ASIC failure raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: LASER_BIAS_HIGH
reference.definition: A minor transmitter-ageing alarm raised when laser bias exceeds its configured high threshold.
reference.example: Laser bias reaches 122% of beginning-of-life current and raises LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

reference.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating that an inline amplifier receives no optical traffic light at its input.
reference.example: A cut ahead of an inline amplifier causes AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: OMS_LOS_P
reference.definition: A critical preamplifier alarm indicating loss of multiplex-section line light at the receiving end.
reference.example: A disconnected receive-side jumper causes the preamplifier to raise OMS_LOS_P.

reference.label: OSC_LOS
reference.definition: A major section alarm indicating that the incoming optical supervisory channel is absent.
reference.example: Excess span loss removes the OSC and the downstream amplifier raises OSC_LOS.

reference.label: AMP_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical amplifier alarm indicating internal failure and absence of output despite available input light.
reference.example: A pump failure leaves an amplifier input present but output dark, triggering AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
reference.definition: A minor amplifier alarm indicating measured gain differs from target by more than the allowed tolerance.
reference.example: An amplifier produces 17.5 dB against a 20 dB target and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
reference.definition: A minor end-of-life alarm raised when normalized pump drive current exceeds its ageing threshold.
reference.example: Pump current reaches 123% and triggers AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: CLIENT_SF
reference.definition: A critical client-port alarm indicating failure of the associated client service.
reference.example: A failed active ODU path causes the client port to raise CLIENT_SF.

reference.label: ODU_AIS
reference.definition: A non-alarming client-port indication that ODU alarm indication signal is being received.
reference.example: A downstream port reports ODU_AIS after upstream OTU frame loss.

reference.label: ODU_BDI
reference.definition: A non-alarming indication that the far end reports an ODU-direction defect or received ODU-AIS.
reference.example: A remote port receives ODU-AIS and returns BDI, causing local ODU_BDI.

reference.label: ODU_TIM
reference.definition: A major alarm indicating that the received ODU trail trace does not match the expected source.
reference.example: A wrongly connected ODU presents an unexpected trace and raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: PROT_ACTIVE
reference.definition: A minor indication that the protection ODU path is currently carrying the service.
reference.example: A working-path failure makes the selector choose protection and raise PROT_ACTIVE.

reference.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
reference.definition: A minor alarm indicating that the protection ODU path is unavailable.
reference.example: The working path remains active while a standby-path cut raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating a hardware failure of the client port.
reference.example: A failed 100GE PHY raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating an internal OTN cross-connect-fabric failure.
reference.example: An OTN switch detects a failed fabric plane and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

reference.label: Single optical channel
reference.definition: Impact limited to one wavelength rather than the complete optical multiplex.
reference.example: A shifted WSS passband degrades channel 37 while adjacent channels remain normal.

reference.label: All optical channels
reference.definition: The complete set of wavelengths carried by an affected unit, span, or ROADM degree.
reference.example: An amplifier output failure removes all channels it carries.

reference.label: Subset of channels
reference.definition: A proper subset of carried wavelengths rather than one channel or the whole multiplex.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens eight band-edge channels but not the other wavelengths.

reference.label: Other channels
reference.definition: Channels outside the specifically affected wavelength, receiver, or ROADM input.
reference.example: A receiver defect affects one channel while the other channels remain normal.

reference.label: Single receiver
reference.definition: Impact restricted to the particular receiving function under diagnosis.
reference.example: Only one coherent receiver reports high pre-FEC BER.

reference.label: Optical path
reference.definition: The end-to-end optical route traversed by a wavelength through fibre and optical elements.
reference.example: Power and OSNR remain normal along the optical path despite a local receiver defect.

reference.label: Single ODU
reference.definition: One Optical Data Unit trail or container rather than all ODUs sharing infrastructure.
reference.example: A wrong cross-connection misroutes one ODU4.

reference.label: All affected ODUs
reference.definition: Every ODU contained in an affected OTU or traversing an affected switch fabric.
reference.example: OTU frame loss inserts AIS into all ODUs carried by the OTU.

reference.label: Client service
reference.definition: The customer-facing traffic service carried through the transport network.
reference.example: A failed client port interrupts one 100GE customer service.

reference.label: Monitoring functions
reference.definition: Equipment status, measurement, and performance-reporting functions.
reference.example: A dead card stops publishing its power and BER measurements.

reference.label: Local equipment
reference.definition: The currently managed node, unit, card, port, or switch rather than a remote point.
reference.example: EQPT_TX_FAIL localizes the laser defect to the current unit.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The receiving endpoint opposite the referenced transmitter.
reference.example: A local laser failure appears as OCH_LOS at the far-end receiver.

reference.label: Far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote transmitter whose signal enters the local receiver.
reference.example: Local OCH_LOS is traced to a failed laser at the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: Upstream optical path
reference.definition: Any earlier point in the optical signal's propagation route relative to the observer.
reference.example: A dirty connector two nodes before the receiver lies upstream on the optical path.

reference.label: Downstream
reference.definition: At a point later in the direction of signal or traffic flow.
reference.example: A WSS attenuation defect is observed as low power at the next downstream node.

reference.label: Incoming fibre section
reference.definition: The fibre span immediately upstream of the observing node or amplifier.
reference.example: OSC_LOS is assigned to the incoming section after a span cut.

reference.label: Preceding amplifier
reference.definition: The nearest upstream optical amplifier feeding the current span or unit.
reference.example: No light reaches the current site because the preceding amplifier failed.

reference.label: Multiplex-section input
reference.definition: The physical entry point where multiplexed optical traffic is launched into or received by a section.
reference.example: A disconnected jumper at the multiplex-section input removes all launched wavelengths.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The ODU route designated as the normal member of a protected pair.
reference.example: A fault on the working ODU path triggers a switch to protection.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU route reserved to protect the working path.
reference.example: A defect on the protection path raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

reference.label: Currently selected ODU path
reference.definition: Whichever working or protection ODU route is currently carrying service traffic.
reference.example: A defect on the selected path interrupts traffic until another path is chosen.

reference.label: OTN switch on ODU path
reference.definition: An intermediate OTN cross-connect traversed by the ODU connection.
reference.example: A wrong mapping in an intermediate switch sends the ODU to the wrong destination.

reference.label: Standard monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring available without a specialized optical-monitoring licence or option.
reference.example: Client errored seconds are supplied in standard 15-minute bins.

reference.label: Power-monitoring option
reference.definition: An entitlement or hardware option exposing optical input, output, or received-power measurements.
reference.example: Enabling power monitoring exposes amplifier composite input and output power.

reference.label: Advanced-monitoring option
reference.definition: An entitlement or capability exposing advanced coherent and equipment-health metrics.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring exposes pre-FEC BER, DGD, polarization rate, and normalized laser currents.

reference.label: Channel-monitoring option
reference.definition: An entitlement or capability exposing per-wavelength power and OSNR measurements.
reference.example: A ROADM with channel monitoring reports power and OSNR for each wavelength.

reference.label: Hard failure
reference.definition: An abrupt and definite loss of required equipment or connectivity function.
reference.example: A dead amplifier immediately removes all output channels.

reference.label: Soft degradation
reference.definition: A partial deterioration in signal or equipment performance while operation may continue.
reference.example: Amplifier noise increases while output power and traffic remain present.

reference.label: Incipient condition
reference.definition: A gradually developing deterioration detectable before a hard failure or end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: Pump drive rises for months while gain remains stable.

reference.label: Post-provisioning error pattern
reference.definition: A fault pattern primarily associated with recent configuration or cross-connection changes.
reference.example: An ODU is delivered to the wrong port immediately after a reroute.

reference.label: Critical
reference.definition: The highest listed alarm class for immediate or substantial loss of equipment, signal, or service function.
reference.example: OCH_LOS is critical because the optical channel is absent at the receiver.

reference.label: Major
reference.definition: A serious alarm class below critical for significant supervisory or connectivity defects.
reference.example: ODU_TIM is major because the received service comes from the wrong ODU source.

reference.label: Minor
reference.definition: A lower alarm class for degradation, ageing, warning, or protection states.
reference.example: AMP_PUMP_EOL is minor because traffic may still be maintained.

reference.label: Not alarmed
reference.definition: A reported consequential or informational indication that does not create an active alarm severity.
reference.example: ODU_AIS is retained as status while the actionable root alarm remains upstream.

reference.label: OTU frame-loss consequent actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, ODU-AIS is inserted on every carried ODU and OTU-BDI is returned toward the source.
reference.example: An OTU carrying four ODUs loses frame, inserts AIS on all four, and returns BDI.

reference.label: Per-section OSC regeneration
reference.definition: Each amplifier site terminates the incoming OSC and originates a separate OSC on the next section.
reference.example: OSC loss on A–B is detected at B while B still launches an OSC toward C.

reference.label: SNCP path selection
reference.definition: A receiving selector chooses between working and protection ODU paths according to detected defects.
reference.example: When the working ODU receives AIS, the selector chooses the defect-free protection ODU.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM switching
reference.definition: A ROADM independently routes each wavelength at an egress degree.
reference.example: One incoming wavelength is sent east while another is sent south.

reference.label: Ingress impairment propagation by channel
reference.definition: An impairment common to a ROADM ingress follows each affected wavelength onto its independently selected onward route.
reference.example: Low OSNR on a west ingress follows one channel north and another east.
